   gh run list -R meadow/events -c 2222222222222222222222222222222222222222 --json databaseId,status,conclusion,workflowName,url

   The target, body, and head remain unchanged. `ci / test` remains binding pending because its matching Actions run is in progress, despite the `CLEAN` merge state.

5. Complete the own-push comment reconciliation reads:

anthropic/claude-opus-5-5.feedback: After gains f3 cleanly: the obstacle template lists eligible numeric deliver and assess, stop recommended last, no fix/wait rows, and the deliver row states that an unchanged src/guard.ts need exits again, so extension alone cannot clear it. But After loses f1 and f2 because step 1 runs a full 15-minute bounded CI watch (minting poll_deadline, running `gh pr checks --watch` to expiry) before the exit check ever looks at the helper's `open - needs` result; the narration explicitly says 'the open P1 blocker does not disable it'. Before kept f1/f2 precisely because its watch guard said a non-empty Blockers list suppresses the watch, so the failed prerequisite went straight to the obstacle report. To keep all three, make the course wording order the own-push re-entry as: (1) read the wave's helper closure results first; if any implementer returned `open - needs <what>` (or any unchanged failed prerequisite), route immediately to the needs obstacle exit with no watch, no repair and no deadline mint; (2) only when no needs obstacle and no open blocker remain does the delivery body enter the binding-CI watch with its own-push-renewed deadline. Also drop the 'CI pending past 15 minutes' secondary prerequisite in this scenario, since it only exists because the watch was wrongly run.

confirmation.feedback: After gets the menu right (eligible numeric deliver and assess, stop recommended last, no fix/wait rows, extension explicitly unable to clear an unchanged need), but it breaks f1 and f2 by running a 15-minute `gh pr checks --watch` (step 1, 'D3 step 4 - Wait course') before the exit check fires on the helper's `open - needs src/guard.ts outside the diff` result; the watch happens between the failed prerequisite and the obstacle report, so the obstacle is no longer the thing that exits first. Before never surfaced an obstacle at all—it treated P1 as an ordinary open blocker, offered a `wait` row and a recommended `fix` row, and asked for a new fix selection—so f1 and f3 clearly failed and f2 had no obstacle report to anchor to. One wording nit for After: the deliver row's phrase 'resume only after the unchanged repair obstacle is cleared' slightly blurs what the pick does; stating it as 'deliver - extend each cumulative cap by six; the needs-src/guard.ts obstacle must still be cleared by a change outside the diff before repair resumes' would make the eligible-but-insufficient nature of the extension unambiguous while keeping every fact intact.
